part.text: {"reframes":[{"bottleneck":"For exchangeable members, fair CRPS/Brier follow skill(M) = skill(∞) + c/M: past ~100 members the curve is a known Monte Carlo decay, so 1,000-member runs mostly re-measure a number already fixed by the 50-member distribution. Compute buys more of the same, and 7 dates cannot show where the asymptote sits.","assumption":"That the saturation point must be located by brute force: run every ensemble size up to 1,000 and read off where the curve flattens.","reframe":"Change what is measured: estimate the asymptote and curvature of skill vs 1/M instead of skill at large M. With exchangeable members both parameters of a + b/M are estimable by bootstrap-subsampling a small archived ensemble. The real question — does shared error cap skill — is about skill(∞) vs a perfect-forecast reference, not about M=1,000.","question":"Does the fitted skill(∞) from 10–50-member bootstrap subsamples of archived AIFS-ENS forecasts fall short of the perfect-forecast fair CRPS for top-percentile wind, temperature, and rain by more than its bootstrap confidence interval — i.e., is the shared-error cap measurable without running a single member past 50?","measure":"Download ECMWF open-data AIFS-ENS 51-member forecasts for ~90 days plus matching ERA5; score top-percentile fair CRPS and Brier; bootstrap member subsamples at sizes 10/20/30/40/50; fit a + b/M per variable; extrapolate to M=1,000 and M=∞. CPU-only, ~1–2 TB storage, roughly $50–100 and a few days, no GPU.","compute_after":"If the extrapolated 50→1,000 gain is below between-date noise, the 7,000-forecast run buys nothing and the budget moves to the date axis; if the asymptote sits measurably above the 50-member curve, one 1,000-member date confirms it — a ~7x cost cut. (The forecast loop itself is chaotic, so guess-the-whole-trajectory parallelism does not apply; members are already side by side, so the only remaining lever is statistical.)","exact":"Fair CRPS(M) = a + b/M fit on 200 bootstrap replicates per date; report a, b, predicted gain ŝ(1000) − ŝ(50) with 95% CI, per variable, over ~90 dates.","expected":"b positive but small; predicted 50→1,000 gain ≈ 0.02·b, likely smaller than the date-to-date standard error on 7 dates — showing the planned test is under-powered on dates, not members.","fails_if":"The a + b/M fit is poor (systematic extra curvature) or the asymptote CI is wider than the hypothesized shared-error gap — then the exchangeable-draw model breaks and full-size runs are needed.","closest_prior":"HENS Part 2's member-subsampling curves over 7,424 SFNO members [s_hens] — apply that analysis to archived AIFS-ENS 51-member output before buying new forecasts."},{"bottleneck":"The rare-extreme claim lives or dies on the number of independent extreme cases. Seven dates yield a handful of top-percentile events, so the standard error of any 50-vs-1,000 skill difference is set by date count; no member count can reduce it.","assumption":"That the unit of work is one member, so more compute should buy more members per date (10→1,000 on 7 dates).","reframe":"Make the unit of work one date. At fixed budget of ~7,000 fifteen-day forecasts, search the (dates × members) grid and pick the allocation that minimizes the standard error of the quantity of interest — skill gain past 50 members — instead of maximizing members per date.","question":"At a fixed budget of ~7,000 forecasts, which (n_dates × members) allocation minimizes the standard error of the estimated fair-CRPS gain between 50 and 200 members for top-percentile wind, temperature, and rain?","measure":"Power analysis from archived data: estimate between-date variance of top-percentile scores from a season of archived 51-member AIFS-ENS (or HENS's 92 dates), combine analytically with the known c/M member-sampling variance, evaluate SE over the allocation grid. CPU-only, tens of dollars, days.","compute_after":"Compute now buys dates — the axis that cuts the dominant variance as 1/√n_dates — rather than members, which hit the 1/M wall; each A100-hour then shrinks the standard error of the skill-gain estimate instead of re-sampling the same exchangeable distribution.","exact":"SE²(gain) = σ²_date·(1/n_50 + 1/n_200) + σ²_member(50, 200); grid n_dates ∈ {7, 14, 28, 56} × members ∈ {50, 100, 200, 500, 1000} with n_dates × members ≈ 7,000; report the minimizing cell.","expected":"The optimum sits near 50–150 members and 50–140 dates, mirroring HENS's 92-date design; the 7 × 1,000 plan is among the worst cells for this question.","fails_if":"Between-date variance of tail scores turns out smaller than member-sampling variance at 50 members (implausible for rare extremes), or members are not exchangeable so the c/M law fails.","closest_prior":"HENS Part 2's 92-date design [s_hens]; fair-score sampling theory (Ferro et al.) giving the c/M member term."},{"bottleneck":"The proposed test measures a symptom — scores flattening in M — on too few cases. The hypothesized cap is a property of the afCRPS-trained predictive distribution's tails, which 1,000 members on 7 dates estimates no better than 50 members on many dates.","assumption":"That 'shared model error caps skill' can only be seen by watching skill flatten as members grow.","reframe":"Change the objective: measure the cap directly as tail calibration of the exchangeable distribution plus tail-error dependence. If pooled members misrepresent ERA5's top-percentile exceedance frequency, skill(∞) is already capped and no member count helps; if calibrated, gains follow the sampling law. Also compute effective ensemble size N_eff = M/(1 + (M−1)ρ) from inter-member tail-error correlation ρ — if ρ > 0, the effective ensemble saturates far below the nominal size.","question":"Over a season of archived AIFS-ENS forecasts, does the pooled-member exceedance frequency at ERA5's 99th percentile match 1% for each variable, and what N_eff does the measured tail-error correlation ρ imply at M = 51?","measure":"From the same archived 51-member season (no GPU): (a) tail reliability — observed vs nominal exceedance ratio with binomial CI at the 99th percentile; (b) ρ̂ from member-error correlations conditioned on grid-point ERA5 exceedances, block-bootstrapped over dates; (c) tail-restricted rank histograms. Tens of dollars, days.","compute_after":"If tails are miscalibrated or N_eff saturates near ~50, the cap is confirmed with zero new GPU spend, and compute should go where it changes the answer: recalibration or tail-weighted fine-tuning of the model (changing the trained distribution), not more draws from it.","exact":"Per variable: exceedance ratio with 95% binomial CI over ~90 days × 51 members; ρ̂_tail with block bootstrap; N_eff(51) = 51/(1 + 50·ρ̂_tail).","expected":"Slight tail under-dispersion or ρ̂_tail ≈ 0.1–0.3 from shared model/initial-condition error, giving N_eff well below 51 — the effective-ensemble ceiling, not the nominal member count, flattens the skill curve.","fails_if":"Tails are calibrated and ρ̂_tail ≈ 0: then the only cap is sampling, the a + b/M law holds, and the honest answer is that 1,000 members help only via the small, predictable variance term.","closest_prior":"HENS Part 2 tail sampling [s_hens]; AIFS-ENS afCRPS evaluation [s_crps_paper]; standard N_eff / ensemble-dressing diagnostics."}]}
